review_notes: I read the whole file. I also read the other uses of largeTupleVector (TailPrimeRegroup, ScaleFirstTuple), the definitions of largePrimeTupleNorm and largePrimeTupleProduct, and Mathlib's Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow. I found no other duplicates. largeTupleIndependentSum and largeTuple_coordinate_support are specific to this argument and have no Mathlib counterpart. One uncertainty: largeTupleVector is a thin, purpose-named wrapper. It may be a deliberate local abbreviation, and the cost of keeping it is modest (one def, three small lemmas, and uses in three files). I report it at moderate confidence.

findings.excerpt:
def largeTupleVector {i j : ℕ} (q : (Fin i → Eisenstein) × (Fin j → Eisenstein)) :
    (Fin i ⊕ Fin j) → Eisenstein := Sum.elim q.1 q.2
findings.problem: largeTupleVector is the inverse direction of Mathlib's Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow (Fin i) (Fin j) Eisenstein, written out as Sum.elim q.1 q.2 and given a local name. largeTupleVector_split is just the right_inv / apply_symm_apply law for that equivalence, proved by hand with funext and cases. The same uncurried Sum.elim is also hand-written in largePrimeTupleNorm. The wrapper therefore re-creates an existing concept, its inverse and its round-trip law. It also loses the Equiv API, which could be used for reindexing sums over the pair type.
findings.proposed_change: Replace largeTupleVector q by (Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow (Fin i) (Fin j) Eisenstein).symm q. Alternatively keep it as an abbrev or notation for that expression, so that the simp lemmas sumArrowEquivProdArrow_symm_apply_inl and _inr and Equiv.apply_symm_apply apply. Then largeTupleVector_split reduces to Equiv.apply_symm_apply, and the norm and product lemmas become short corollaries.
findings.benefit: The file would reuse Mathlib's equivalence and its simp lemmas instead of a private copy. That drops one definition and one lemma, and the same change simplifies the call sites in TailPrimeRegroup.lean and ScaleFirstTuple.lean. A reader would also recognise the Sum/Prod reindexing at once.

evidence.excerpt: def sumArrowEquivProdArrow (α β γ : Type*) : (α ⊕ β → γ) ≃ (α → γ) × (β → γ) :=
((sumArrowEquivProdArrow α β γ).symm (f, g)) (inl a) = f a
Sum.elim (fun a => norm (q.1 a)) (fun b => norm (q.2 b))
